name: Leiothrichidae
description: Leiothrichidae is a large and diverse family of passerine birds found primarily in Asia. They include the laughingthrushes, mesias, minlas, and sibias, known for their often colorful plumage and loud, musical calls.

children.name: Grammatoptila
children.description: A monotypic genus of laughingthrush with boldly striped plumage, found in the Himalayas.

children.name: Grammatoptila striata
children.description: The striated laughingthrush (Grammatoptila striata) is a passerine bird in the family Leiothrichidae.

children.name: Pterorhinus
children.description: A genus of medium to large laughingthrushes with varied plumage, found across East and Southeast Asia.

children.name: Pterorhinus pectoralis
children.description:
The greater necklaced laughingthrush (Pterorhinus pectoralis) is a species of passerine bird in the family Leiothrichidae. It is found in Bangladesh, Bhutan, China, India, Laos, Myanmar, Nepal, Thailand and Vietnam. It is introduced to Hawaii. Its natural habitats are subtropical or tropical moist lowland forest and subtropical or tropical moist montane forest.
This species was formerly placed in the genus Garrulax but following the publication of a comprehensive molecular phylogenetic study in 2018, it was moved to the resurrected genus Pterorhinus.

children.name: Pterorhinus chinensis
children.description: The black-throated laughingthrush (Pterorhinus chinensis) is a species of bird in the family Leiothrichidae. It is found in Cambodia, China, Laos, Myanmar, Thailand, and Vietnam. Its natural habitats are subtropical or tropical moist lowland forest and subtropical or tropical moist montane forest, mostly at submontane to montane elevations.

children.name: Pterorhinus albogularis
children.description:
The white-throated laughingthrush (Pterorhinus albogularis) is a species of passerine bird in the family Leiothrichidae. It is found mainly in the northern regions of the Indian subcontinent, primarily the Himalayas, and some adjoining and disjunct areas. It ranges across Afghanistan, Bhutan, India, Myanmar, Nepal, Tibet and Vietnam. Its natural habitat is subtropical or tropical moist montane forests.
This species was formerly placed in the genus Garrulax but following the publication of a comprehensive molecular phylogenetic study in 2018, it was moved to the resurrected genus Pterorhinus.

children.name: Pterorhinus monileger
children.description: A laughingthrush with a narrow black necklace, grey upperparts, and white underparts. It ranges from the Himalayas through Southeast Asia to southern China.

children.name: Pterorhinus mitratus
children.description:
The chestnut-capped laughingthrush (Pterorhinus mitratus), also known as the spectacled laughingthrush, is a species of bird in the family Leiothrichidae. It is found in Sumatra (Indonesia) and the Thai-Malay Peninsula. Its natural habitats are subtropical or tropical moist lowland forests and subtropical or tropical moist montane forests. The chestnut-hooded laughingthrush was previously considered a subspecies.
The chestnut-capped laughingthrush was formerly placed in the genus Garrulax but following the publication of a comprehensive molecular phylogenetic study in 2018, it was moved to the resurrected genus Pterorhinus.

children.name: Pterorhinus lanceolatus
children.description: The Chinese babax (Pterorhinus lanceolatus) is a species of bird in the family Leiothrichidae.

children.name: Pterorhinus waddelli
children.description: The giant babax (Pterorhinus waddelli) is a species of bird in the laughingthrush family Leiothrichidae, found in northeast India and southern Tibet.

children.name: Pterorhinus koslowi
children.description: The Tibetan babax (Pterorhinus koslowi) is a species of bird in the family Leiothrichidae.

children.name: Pterorhinus ruficollis
children.description: The rufous-necked laughingthrush (Pterorhinus ruficollis) is a bird species in the laughingthrush family, Leiothrichidae. It is found in Bangladesh, Bhutan, China, India, Myanmar and Nepal, where its natural habitats are subtropical or tropical moist lowland forest and subtropical or tropical moist montane forest. Little study was done on this species due to its abundance and lack of interest in its conservation.

children.name: Pterorhinus nigrimentum
children.description: A laughingthrush with a black chin, white face, chestnut crown, and olive-brown body. It inhabits montane forests of southern China and northern Vietnam.

children.name: Pterorhinus poecilorhynchus
children.description: The rusty laughingthrush (Pterorhinus poecilorhynchus) is a species of bird in the family Leiothrichidae.

children.name: Pterorhinus caerulatus
children.description:
The grey-sided laughingthrush (Pterorhinus caerulatus) is a species of passerine bird in the family Leiothrichidae.
This species was formerly placed in the genus Garrulax but following the publication of a comprehensive molecular phylogenetic study in 2018, it was moved to the resurrected genus Pterorhinus.

children.name: Garrulax
children.description: A genus of striking laughingthrushes with bold head patterns, found in Asia.

children.name: Garrulax leucolophus
children.description: The white-crested laughingthrush (Garrulax leucolophus) is a member of the family Leiothrichidae. It is a highly social and vocal bird found in forest and scrub from the Himalayan foothills to Southeast Asia.

children.name: Garrulax bicolor
children.description: The Sumatran laughingthrush (Garrulax bicolor), also known as the black-and-white laughingthrush, is a member of the family Leiothrichidae.

children.name: Garrulax strepitans
children.description: The white-necked laughingthrush (Garrulax strepitans) is a species of bird in the family Leiothrichidae. It is found in Yunnan, Laos, Myanmar and Thailand. Its natural habitats are subtropical or tropical moist lowland forests and subtropical or tropical moist montane forests.

children.name: Garrulax ferrugineus
children.description: A laughingthrush with a rufous forehead and crown, grey face, and olive-brown body. It inhabits montane forests of the eastern Himalayas.

children.name: Garrulax leucogaster
children.description: A laughingthrush with a white belly, chestnut crown, black mask, and grey upperparts. It is found in the mountains of southern India.

children.name: Garrulax maurus
children.description: A laughingthrush with a chestnut back and wings, white face, black mask, and grey underparts. It is endemic to the mountains of Sumatra.

children.name: Ianthocincla
children.description: A genus of colourful laughingthrushes with distinctive facial patterns and spotted or ocellated plumage. They are found in montane forests of the Himalayas and China.

children.name: Ianthocincla rufogularis
children.description: The rufous-chinned laughingthrush (Ianthocincla rufogularis) is a bird species in the family Leiothrichidae. It ranges across the northern parts of the Indian subcontinent and some parts of Southeast Asia.

children.name: Ianthocincla konkakinhensis
children.description:
The chestnut-eared laughingthrush (Ianthocincla konkakinhensis) is a species of bird in the family Leiothrichidae. It is found in Vietnam and possibly Laos.
This species measures. This laughingthrush has boldly and irregularly barred black and white upperparts, a black-streaked grey forehead, chestnut ear-coverts, and a white-tipped tail with a broad black sub-terminal band.

children.name: Ianthocincla ocellata
children.description: The spotted laughingthrush (Ianthocincla ocellata) is a bird species in the family Leiothrichidae.

children.name: Ianthocincla bieti
children.description:
The white-speckled laughingthrush (Ianthocincla bieti), also known as Biet's Laughingthrush, is a species of passerine bird in the family Leiothrichidae. It is endemic to China. Its natural habitat is temperate forests. It is threatened by habitat loss.
The white-speckled laughingthrush was at one time placed in the genus Garrulax but following the publication of a comprehensive molecular phylogenetic study in 2018, it was moved to the resurrected genus Ianthocincla. The specific name commemorates the French missionary to China Félix Biet.

children.name: Leiothrix
children.description: A genus of brightly colored, small to medium-sized birds with melodious songs, found in Asia.

children.name: Leiothrix argentauris
children.description: The silver-eared mesia (Leiothrix argentauris) is a species of bird from South East Asia.

children.name: Leiothrix lutea
children.description: The red-billed leiothrix (Leiothrix lutea) is a member of the family Leiothrichidae, native to southern China and the Himalayas. Adults have bright red bills and a dull yellow ring around their eyes. Their backs are dull olive green, and they have a bright yellow-orange throat with a yellow chin; females are somewhat duller than males, and juveniles have black bills. It has also been introduced in various parts of the world, with small populations of escapees having existed in Japan since the 1980s. It has become a common cagebird and amongst aviculturists it goes by various names: Pekin robin, Pekin nightingale, Japanese nightingale, and Japanese (hill) robin, the last two being misnomers as it is not native to Japan (although it has been introduced and naturalised there).

children.name: Actinodura
children.description: A genus of small to medium-sized birds including minlas and barwings, found in montane forests of Asia.

children.name: Actinodura cyanouroptera
children.description:
The blue-winged minla (Actinodura cyanouroptera), also known as the blue-winged siva, is a species of bird in the family Leiothrichidae.
It has in the past been placed in the genus Minla and also in the monotypic Siva.

children.name: Actinodura egertoni
children.description:
The rusty-fronted barwing (Actinodura egertoni) is a species of bird in the laughingthrush family, Leiothrichidae.
It is found in Southeast Asia from the Himalayas to north-eastern Myanmar. Its natural habitats are temperate forests and subtropical or tropical moist montane forests.

children.name: Actinodura ramsayi
children.description: The spectacled barwing (Actinodura ramsayi) is a species of bird in the family Leiothrichidae.

children.name: Actinodura souliei
children.description: The streaked barwing (Actinodura souliei) is a species of bird in the family Leiothrichidae.

children.name: Actinodura morrisoniana
children.description: The Taiwan barwing or Formosan barwing (Actinodura morrisoniana) is a species of bird in the family Leiothrichidae.

children.name: Actinodura waldeni
children.description:
The streak-throated barwing (Actinodura waldeni) is a species of bird in the family Leiothrichidae. It is found in western Yunnan, southern Tibet, Northeast India and Myanmar.
Its natural habitat is subtropical or tropical moist montane forest.

children.name: Actinodura nipalensis
children.description: The hoary-throated barwing (Actinodura nipalensis) is a species of bird in the family Leiothrichidae. It is found in along the northern parts of the Indian subcontinent, primarily in the Eastern Himalayas, and ranges across Bhutan, India, Tibet, and Nepal. Its natural habitats are temperate forest and subtropical or tropical moist montane forest.

children.name: Actinodura strigula
children.description:
The bar-throated minla or chestnut-tailed minla (Actinodura strigula), or even bar-throated siva, is a species of bird in the laughingthrush and babbler family Leiothrichidae. Traditionally, it has been placed in the genus Minla but is now placed in Actinodura.
The species is found in montane forest from India to Malaysia.

children.name: Actinodura sodangorum
children.authorship: J. C. Eames, Trai Trong Le, Nguyen Cu & Eve, 1998

children.name: Minla
children.description: A monotypic genus containing the Red-tailed Minla, a colourful bird of montane forests in East Asia.

children.name: Minla ignotincta
children.description:
The red-tailed minla (Minla ignotincta) is a passerine bird in the family Leiothrichidae. It is the only species in the genus Minla.
It is found in the Indian subcontinent and Southeast Asia. Its range includes Bangladesh, Bhutan, India, Laos, Myanmar, Nepal, Thailand and Vietnam. Its natural habitat is subtropical or tropical moist montane forests.

children.name: Trochalopteron
children.description: A genus of colorful laughingthrushes with scaled or patterned plumage, found in montane forests of Asia.

children.name: Trochalopteron affine
children.description: The black-faced laughingthrush (Trochalopteron affine) is a bird species in the family Leiothrichidae. It is found in the Eastern Himalayas. Its range extends from eastern Nepal eastwards to Arunachal Pradesh in India and further to Myanmar, along with Bhutan and southeastern Tibet. Small disjunct populations also exist in continental Southeast Asia.

children.name: Trochalopteron squamatum
children.description: The blue-winged laughingthrush (Trochalopteron squamatum) is a bird in the family Leiothrichidae. It is found in Eastern Himalaya, Yunnan, Myanmar and Laos where its natural habitat is the dense undergrowth of subtropical or tropical moist broadleaved evergreen montane forests.

children.name: Trochalopteron subunicolor
children.description: The scaly laughingthrush (Trochalopteron subunicolor) is a bird species in the family Leiothrichidae.

children.name: Trochalopteron ocellatum
children.description: The Spotted Laughingthrush has dark plumage with prominent white spots on the breast and head, and rufous-tinged wings. It inhabits rhododendron and oak forests in the Himalayas.

children.name: Trochalopteron erythrocephalum
children.description:
The chestnut-crowned laughingthrush (Trochalopteron erythrocephalum) is a species of bird in the family Leiothrichidae. It is found in Bhutan, China, India, Pakistan and Nepal.
The silver-eared laughingthrush, formerly included as a subspecies, is now usually regarded as a separate species.

children.name: Trochalopteron formosum
children.description:
The red-winged laughingthrush (Trochalopteron formosum) is a bird species in the family Leiothrichidae.
The plumage is mostly brown with large areas of red in the wings and tail. The crown and ear-coverts are grey with dark streaks and the throat is dark. The bill and feet are blackish. It has a loud, whistling song and is 27 to 28 centimetres (11 inches) long. The red-tailed laughingthrush is similar but has a rufous crown and greyer back and breast.

children.name: Trochalopteron milnei
children.description: The red-tailed laughingthrush (Trochalopteron milnei) is a species of bird in the laughingthrush family Leiothrichidae. It is found in the montane forests of Myanmar, Laos, southern China and central Vietnam.

children.name: Trochalopteron melanostigma
children.description: The silver-eared laughingthrush (Trochalopteron melanostigma) is a species of bird in the family Leiothrichidae. It is found in southern Yunnan, Laos, Myanmar, Thailand and Vietnam. It was formerly considered a subspecies of the chestnut-crowned laughingthrush, G. Erythrocephalus.

children.name: Trochalopteron chrysopterum
children.description: The Assam laughingthrush (Trochalopteron chrysopterum) is a species of bird in the family Leiothrichidae.

children.name: Trochalopteron imbricatum
children.description: The Bhutan laughingthrush (Trochalopteron imbricatum) is a species of bird in the family Leiothrichidae.

children.name: Trochalopteron lineatum
children.description: The streaked laughingthrush (Trochalopteron lineatum) is a species of bird in the family Leiothrichidae.

children.name: Trochalopteron austeni
children.description: The brown-capped laughingthrush (Trochalopteron austeni) is a species of bird in the family Leiothrichidae. It is found in the Patkai range, where its natural habitat is subtropical and tropical moist montane forests.

children.name: Trochalopteron elliotii
children.description:
Elliot's laughingthrush (Trochalopteron elliotii) is a bird species in the family Leiothrichidae.
It is found in central China and far northeastern India, in shrubs and in forests with a combination of coniferous and deciduous trees.

children.name: Trochalopteron ludlowi
children.description: A laughingthrush with a grey crown, black mask, olive-brown body, and rufous wings. It is found in the mountains of northeastern India and adjacent Tibet.

children.name: Trochalopteron meridionale
children.description: The Ashambu laughingthrush or Travancore laughingthrush (Montecincla meridionalis) is a species of bird in the family Leiothrichidae.

children.name: Trochalopteron ngoclinhense
children.description:
The golden-winged laughingthrush (Trochalopteron ngoclinhense) is a species of bird in the family Leiothrichidae. It is endemic to Ngọc Linh mountain (southwestern Vietnam).
Its natural habitat is subtropical or tropical moist montane forests. It is threatened by habitat loss.
children.authorship: (J. C. Eames, Trai Trong Le & Nguyen Cu, 1999)

children.name: Trochalopteron virgatum
children.description: The striped laughingthrush (Trochalopteron virgatum) is a species of bird in the family Leiothrichidae.

children.name: Heterophasia
children.description: A genus of slender, long-tailed birds with melodious songs, known as sibias, found in montane forests of Asia.

children.name: Heterophasia capistrata
children.description: The rufous sibia (Heterophasia capistrata) is a species of bird in the family Leiothrichidae.

children.name: Heterophasia gracilis
children.description: The grey sibia (Heterophasia gracilis) is a species of bird in the family Leiothrichidae.

children.name: Heterophasia pulchella
children.description: The beautiful sibia (Heterophasia pulchella) is a species of bird in the family Leiothrichidae.

children.name: Heterophasia desgodinsi
children.description:
The black-headed sibia (Heterophasia desgodinsi) is a bird species in the family Leiothrichidae. In former times it was often included with the dark-backed sibia in H. Melanoleuca. Together with most other sibias, it is sometimes separated in the genus Malacias.
It is found in China, Laos and Vietnam. Its natural habitat is subtropical or tropical moist montane forests.

children.name: Heterophasia melanoleuca
children.description: The dark-backed sibia (Heterophasia melanoleuca) is a bird species in the family Leiothrichidae. In former times it was included the black-headed sibia, H. Desgodinsi. Together with most other sibias, it is sometimes separated in the genus Malacias. It is found in China, Myanmar and Thailand. Its natural habitat is subtropical or tropical moist montane forests.

children.name: Heterophasia picaoides
children.description: The long-tailed sibia (Heterophasia picaoides) is a species of Leiothrichidae from Southeast Asia. The species was once placed in the large family Timaliidae, but that family is sometimes split with this species being placed with the laughingthrushes in the family Leiothrichidae. The species is sometimes treated as the only species in the genus Heterophasia, with the other species being placed in the genus Malacias.

children.name: Laniellus
children.description: A small genus of strikingly patterned birds with spotted and streaked plumage, found in montane forests of Southeast Asia. They are related to the sibias and have long, graduated tails.

children.name: Laniellus albonotatus
children.description: The spotted crocias (Laniellus albonotatus) is a passerine bird in the family Leiothrichidae.

children.name: Laniellus langbianis
children.description:
The grey-crowned crocias (Laniellus langbianis) is a passerine bird in the family Leiothrichidae. It is endemic to Vietnam, where it has a highly restricted distribution in the Da Lat Plateau. It has also been observed, and independently surveyed in 2015, in Central Vietnam on the Kontum Plateau, where it may be more abundant. Its natural habitat is intact broadleaf evergreen forest and secondary forest, generally near watercourses, between 910–1450 m above sea-level.
This species was formerly placed in the genus Crocias but under the rules of the International Code of Zoological Nomenclature Laniellus Swainson, 1832 has priority over Crocias Temminck, 1836.

children.name: Cutia
children.description: A genus of strikingly patterned birds with barred underparts, found in montane forests of Asia.

children.name: Cutia nipalensis
children.description: The Himalayan cutia (Cutia nipalensis) is a bird species in the family Leiothrichidae.

children.name: Cutia legalleni
children.description: The Vietnamese cutia (Cutia legalleni) is a bird species in the family Leiothrichidae.

children.name: Monteincila
children.description: A small genus of laughingthrushes with rufous and grey plumage, found in the mountains of Southeast Asia.

children.name: Monteincila merulina
children.description: A laughingthrush with a white throat and breast, chestnut crown, and olive-brown upperparts. It is found in montane forests of Sumatra and the Malay Peninsula.

children.name: Leucodioptron
children.description: A genus of laughingthrushes with distinctive white or red markings on the face, found in the mountains of East and Southeast Asia.

children.name: Leucodioptron canorum
children.description: The Chinese hwamei or melodious laughingthrush (Garrulax canorus) is a passerine bird of eastern Asia in the laughingthrush family Leiothrichidae.

children.name: Leucodioptron taewanum
children.description: The Taiwan hwamei (Garrulax taewanus) is a passerine bird in the family Leiothrichidae.

children.name: Turdoides
children.description: A genus of medium-sized laughingthrushes with plain or streaked brown plumage, found in scrub and open woodlands of Asia.

children.name: Turdoides nipalensis
children.description: The spiny babbler (Turdoides nipalensis) is a species of bird in the family Leiothrichidae.

children.name: Turdoides caudata
children.description: The common babbler (Argya caudata) is a member of the family of Leiothrichidae.

children.name: Turdoides malcomi
children.description: A large grey babbler with a pale yellow eye, white throat, and long tail. It is found in dry scrub and open woodlands of the Indian subcontinent.

children.name: Argya
children.description: A genus of medium to large babblers with plain or streaked plumage, found in scrub and grasslands of Asia. They are highly social, often moving in noisy flocks through their habitat.

children.name: Argya caranulata
children.description: A small babbler with tawny underparts, streaked brown upperparts, and a yellow eye. It is found in scrub and grasslands of southern India and Sri Lanka.

children.name: Argya cinereiceps
children.description: A babbler with a grey head, brown upperparts, and buffy underparts. It is endemic to the Western Ghats of India.

children.name: Argya striata
children.description: The jungle babbler (Argya striata) is a member of the family Leiothrichidae found in the Indian subcontinent.

children.name: Argya rufescens
children.description:
The orange-billed babbler (Argya rufescens), also known as Ceylon rufous babbler or Sri Lankan rufous babbler, is a member of the family Leiothrichidae.
The orange-billed babbler is a resident breeding bird endemic to Sri Lanka. In the past, it was considered to be a race of jungle babbler, Argya striata.

children.name: Argya affinis
children.description: The yellow-billed babbler (Argya affinis) is a member of the family Leiothrichidae endemic to southern India and Sri Lanka. The yellow-billed babbler is a common resident breeding bird in Sri Lanka and southern India. Its habitat is scrub, cultivation and garden land. This species, like most babblers, is not migratory, and has short rounded wings and a weak flight and is usually seen calling and foraging in groups. It is often mistaken for the jungle babbler, whose range overlaps in parts of southern India, although it has a distinctive call and tends to be found in more vegetated habitats. Its name is also confused with Turdoides leucocephala, which is also known as white-headed babbler.

children.name: Argya gularis
children.description:
The white-throated babbler (Argya gularis) is a species of bird in the family Leiothrichidae. It is endemic to Myanmar.
This species was formerly placed in the genus Turdoides but following the publication of a comprehensive molecular phylogenetic study in 2018, it was moved to the resurrected genus Argya.

children.name: Chatarrhaea
children.description: A small genus of babblers found in scrub and grasslands of Asia, with plain brown or grey plumage and long tails.

children.name: Chatarrhaea earlei
children.description: A babbler with heavy pale streaking on the brown upperparts, white underparts, and a long tail. It is found in reed beds and grasslands of the Indus and Ganges river systems.

children.name: Acroptila
children.description: A genus of babblers found in scrub and forests of Asia, with plain or slightly streaked plumage.

children.name: Acroptila albiventris
children.description: A small babbler with a white belly, grey head, brown upperparts, and a short tail. It is endemic to the hills of southern India and Sri Lanka.

children.name: Lanioplus
children.description: A genus of small babblers with rufous and white plumage, found in the Himalayas and Southeast Asia.

children.name: Lanioplus rufiscapilla
children.description: A small babbler with a rufous crown, white underparts, brown upperparts, and a long tail. It is found in scrub and forests of the Indian subcontinent.

children.name: Grammatopia
children.description: A genus of babblers with bold streaking on the head and breast, found in the Himalayas and China.

children.name: Grammatopia striata
children.description: A babbler with heavy white streaking on the brown head and breast, brown upperparts, and a long tail. It is found in scrub and grasslands of the Himalayas and southern China.

children.name: Melanocichla
children.description: A small genus of bold black-and-white laughingthrushes with stout, curved bills. They are found in limestone karst forests of Southeast Asia and are known for their loud, ringing calls.

children.name: Melanocichla macrodactyla
children.description: A large black babbler with a white head and throat, a stout curved bill, and a long tail. It is found in limestone karst forests of Thailand, Myanmar, and Indochina.

children.name: Melanocichla calva
children.description:
The bare-headed laughingthrush (Melanocichla calva) is a species of bird in the Old World babbler family Timaliidae. It is endemic to highland forests at elevations of in the mountain ranges of north-central Borneo, along with some outlying peaks. It is long, with both sexes similar in appearance. The head is brownish to greenish yellow and featherless. The area along the lower mandible has a bluish tinge. The rest of the body is dull blackish-brown tinged with grey. Juveniles have more feathers on the head, extending from the forehead to the.
Described by the British ornithologist Richard Bowdler Sharpe in 1888, the bare-headed laughingthrush was then treated as a subspecies of the black laughingthrush from 1935 to 2006, when it was restored to full species status. It feeds on insects such as crickets, cicadas, and ants in dense columns of vegetation formed by vines growing around trees. Although it is classified as being of least concern by the International Union for Conservation of Nature, it is threatened by habitat destruction and fragmentation and its population is thought to be decreasing.

children.name: Sibia
children.description: A genus of long-tailed, melodious birds found in montane forests of Asia. They forage actively in the canopy, often in mixed-species flocks, and are known for their clear, whistled songs.

children.name: Sibia nigriceps
children.description: A sibia with a black cap, blue-grey upperparts, chestnut tail and underparts, and white wing patches. It is found in montane forests of the Himalayas.

children.name: Sibia leucocephala
children.description: A sibia with a white crown, black face, blue-grey upperparts, and chestnut underparts. It is endemic to the mountains of Borneo.

children.name: Leioptila
children.description: A monotypic genus of sibia with a rufous back and black-and-white head pattern, found in the eastern Himalayas.

children.name: Leioptila annectens
children.description:
The rufous-backed sibia (Leioptila annectens) is a passerine bird in the family Leiothrichidae.
It was formerly placed in the genus Heterophasia but is now the only species in the genus Leioptila.

children.name: Malacocincla
children.description: A genus of small, short-tailed babblers with rufous and grey plumage, found in forests of Southeast Asia. They are shy, secretive birds that forage on the forest floor.

children.name: Malacocincla aspera
children.description: A babbler with a rough, spiky crest, brown upperparts, and pale underparts. It is found in lowland forests of Thailand and Myanmar.

children.name: Pellorneum
children.description: A genus of ground-dwelling babblers with streaked or spotted plumage, found in forests of Asia. They are secretive birds that forage in leaf litter, often cocking their tails upward.

children.name: Pellorneum palustre
children.description: The marsh babbler (Pellorneum palustre) is a member of the family Pellorneidae.

children.name: Pellorneum nigriceps
children.description: A babbler with a black crown, white face, brown upperparts, and white underparts. It is endemic to the forests of Borneo.

children.name: Trichastoma
children.description: A genus of medium-sized babblers with plain brown plumage and long tails, found in forests of Southeast Asia.

children.name: Trichastoma bicolor
children.description: The ferruginous babbler (Pellorneum bicolor) is a species of bird in the family Pellorneidae.

children.name: Trichastoma celebense
children.description: The Sulawesi babbler (Pellorneum celebense) is a species of bird in the family Pellorneidae.

children.name: Napothera
children.description: A genus of small, short-tailed babblers with rufous and grey plumage, found in montane forests of Asia. They are often difficult to observe as they forage in dense undergrowth.

children.name: Napothera crassior
children.description: A small babbler with rich brown upperparts, white throat, and rufous underparts. It is endemic to the mountains of Borneo.

children.name: Napothera rajah
children.description: A small babbler with brown upperparts, white underparts heavily scaled with black, and a white supercilium. It is found in montane forests of Borneo.

children.name: Stachyris
children.description: A genus of medium-sized babblers with rufous, grey, and olive plumage, found in forests of Asia. They are active, social birds that forage in noisy flocks in the undergrowth.

children.name: Dumeticola
children.description: A genus of small, secretive babblers with streaked brown plumage, found in dense grasslands and scrub of Asia.

children.name: Dumeticola thoracica
children.description: A small babbler with streaked brown upperparts, white underparts spotted with black, and a white supercilium. It is found in grasslands of the eastern Himalayas and China.

children.name: Dumeticola davidi
children.description: A small babbler with brown upperparts, pale underparts, and a prominent white supercilium. It is found in reed beds and grasslands of East Asia.

children.name: Dumeticola striata
children.description: A babbler with heavily streaked upperparts, white underparts, and a long tail. It is found in grasslands and scrub of the Himalayas and southern China.

children.name: Erophila
children.description: A genus of colourful laughingthrushes with bright rufous or chestnut plumage, found in the mountains of China and the Himalayas.

children.name: Erophila erythrocephala
children.description: A laughingthrush with a chestnut crown, black mask, and olive-brown body. It is found in montane forests of the eastern Himalayas.

children.name: Erophila rufogularis
children.description: A laughingthrush with a rufous throat, grey crown, and olive-brown body. It is found in montane forests of the Himalayas.

children.name: Cinclosoma
children.description: A genus of terrestrial birds with subtly patterned plumage, found in arid and semi-arid regions of Australia. They are shy, ground-dwelling birds that run rather than fly when disturbed.

children.name: Cinclosoma castanotum
children.description: The chestnut quail-thrush (Cinclosoma castanotum) is a native Australian bird of the family Cinclosomatidae. These scrub birds are endemic to Australia and found in all states - barring Tasmania. They are relatively uncommon and are isolated to the semi-arid and arid fringes of the Australian interior.

children.name: Cinclosoma castaneum
children.description: A quail-thrush with a rich chestnut back, black-and-white facial pattern, and pale underparts. It is found in arid scrublands of central Australia.

children.name: Cinclosoma cinnamomeum
children.description: The cinnamon quail-thrush (Cinclosoma cinnamomeum) is a small to medium-sized species of bird that is endemic to Australia. This bird is found in the arid and semi-arid regions of central Australia.

children.name: Cinclosoma albogularis
children.description: A quail-thrush with a white throat, brown upperparts spotted with black, and grey underparts. It is found in dry forests of northern Australia.

children.name: Psophodes
children.description: A genus of Australian birds with distinctive, loud calls that often resemble whipcracks or whistles. They are ground-foraging birds with long, cocked tails and strong legs.

children.name: Psophodes crepitans
children.description: A secretive bird with a black crest and breast, olive-green body, and a long tail. It is famous for its whip-crack song, often sung as a duet.

children.name: Sphenostoma
children.description: A monotypic genus of Australian bird with a distinctive wedge-shaped bill and loud, whistling calls. It inhabits arid and semi-arid scrublands.

children.name: Sphenostoma cristatum
children.description: A bird with a short crest, grey-brown upperparts, white throat, and black breast band. Its far-carrying, bell-like song is a characteristic sound of the Australian outback.

children.name: Coracina
children.description: A large genus of medium-sized birds with grey, black, and white plumage, found across Asia and Australasia. They are arboreal insectivores with a hooked bill.

children.name: Coracina melano
children.description: A cuckooshrike with grey upperparts, white underparts, and black wings. It is found in forests of South and Southeast Asia.

children.name: Coracina novaeguineae
children.description: A cuckooshrike with grey upperparts, white underparts, and black wings. It is found in forests of New Guinea.

children.name: Coracina atakamensis
children.description: A cuckooshrike with dark grey plumage and a black mask. It is found in montane forests of Southeast Asia.

children.name: Garrodia
children.description: A small genus of Asian babblers with plain brown plumage, found in forests of the eastern Himalayas and Southeast Asia.

children.name: Garrodia subtilis
children.description: A plain brown babbler with a pale throat and belly, and a long tail. It is found in forests of the eastern Himalayas.

children.name: Garrodia leucocrypta
children.description: A babbler with a white breast and throat, brown upperparts, and a long tail. It is found in forests of Southeast Asia.
